intro: The Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma — St Jude (Murphy) Stage is a oncology scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Paediatric NHL staging (Toronto Tier 1). It scores 1 criteria and interprets the total across 4 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in oncology
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 1 criteria: Extent of disease. Totals are then banded: 1 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - limited disease; excellent prognosis with short-course therapy; 2 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - limited disease, generally treated on low-risk protocols; 3 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - advanced disease requiring intensified multi-agent chemotherapy; 4 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - CNS and/or marrow involvement. Highest-intensity therapy with CNS-directed treatment; marrow blasts ≥25 % is classified as leukaemia instead.
guidelineRefs: Source (staging): Murphy SB. Classification, staging and end results of treatment of childhood non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Semin Oncol 1980;7:332-9.
Source: Gupta S, Aitken JF, Bartels U et al. Paediatric cancer stage in population-based cancer registries: the Toronto consensus principles and guidelines. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:e163-72.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma — St Jude (Murphy) Stage use?
What do the bands of the Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma — St Jude (Murphy) Stage mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: 1 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - limited disease; excellent prognosis with short-course therapy; 2 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - limited disease, generally treated on low-risk protocols; 3 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - advanced disease requiring intensified multi-agent chemotherapy; 4 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - CNS and/or marrow involvement. Highest-intensity therapy with CNS-directed treatment; marrow blasts ≥25 % is classified as leukaemia instead.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.

faqs.q: Where does this score come from?
faqs.a: Source (staging): Murphy SB. Classification, staging and end results of treatment of childhood non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Semin Oncol 1980;7:332-9.
